content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** Section 6 ("Exclusivity") contains a genuine customer-side restrictive covenant at §6.1 — the Company cannot participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products for the full term (one year, auto-renewing annually under §4.1), and HDI is granted the exclusive right to use our own "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site. There is no automatic performance-based exit (§1.6 is only a discretionary termination right for a late launch), and the closeout carve-out in §6.2 does not cure it. That is walk-away exclusive dealing, so I classified it as a deviation.

§6.3 (HDI restricted from similar projects) runs against the counterparty and benefits us, so it was left untouched, as was the non-exclusive trademark licence in §6.1's second paragraph. The redline is a single surgical replacement of §6.1 delivering the preferred position, with the fallback (12 months, Deerskin Products only, auto-ending on service level/delivery failures) offered in the comment.
